data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Wart & antiviral agents_

**Class:** Iodinated thymidine analogue (first antiviral drug)

## Mechanism of action
- Incorporated into viral (and host) DNA instead of thymidine → faulty DNA → inhibits replication of HSV and VZV; toxic systemically

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Historic: herpes simplex keratitis (eye drops), herpes labialis and zoster (5–40% in DMSO) — replaced by acyclovir

## Dose & formulations
- Historic topical application several times daily

## Adverse effects
- Irritation, contact dermatitis; systemic toxicity (marrow) — topical only

## Contraindications
- Systemic use

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid.

## Viva points
- First antiviral (1962) — now obsolete

_Sources: Khopkar ch.20 (Idoxuridine). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
